title: The bells rung for Niall
summary: The bells of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg are rung a full day and a night for Niall's death, and the capital keeps no market. The crowd that gathers is the largest since his crowning; it stays quiet, and disperses before the second night.

title: The council's oath sworn afresh
summary: Comhairle na Rìoghachd, sitting on its fixed day within the week of the crowning, swears its oath of service afresh before Brìghde. The minute-book gives it one line among the day's ordinary business and no more.

title: The corrected proclamation at Ros dhomhain
summary: A harbour clerk at Ros dhomhain, copying the crowning's proclamation for the gate, writes Niall's name from habit, scores it through, and sets Brìghde's above the line. The corrected copy is kept under glass at the gate.

title: Gormshuil's struck drafts
summary: The chronicler writes and rejects three entries for the crowning before any stands: one too bare, one that says more than an office should say first, one left unfinished as an argument rather than a record. All three are struck through in her working book.

title: Gormshuil's resolve on the one idiom
summary: Having let *mar a thàinig Niall* into the royal record, the chronicler resolves to admit no other such phrase for as long as the office is hers, having seen other offices lose their plainness one borrowed ornament at a time.

title: The hall raised at Seann Dunn
summary: Forty households of the Seann Spioradan along the east coast raise a common hall at Seann Dunn in a single season, working the stone by day, and roof it before the first frost. It holds no image or carving, only two hearths.

title: Gormshuil's visit to the first naming
summary: The chronicler rides east to Seann Dunn to watch the hall's first naming of ancestors, not on an Leabharlann's business but her own, her mother's house keeping the same rite at a hearth too small for half its dead.

title: An Leabharlann's offer to Seann Dunn
summary: Asked by an elder of the hall whether an Leabharlann keeps such lists of the dead, Gormshuil answers that it does not, but will keep any copy sent to it as carefully as anything else that reaches Muileann chaol.

title: The Seann Dunn list first copied to an Leabharlann
summary: The hall at Seann Dunn sends an Leabharlann the first copy of its naming, and goes on sending one every year after, each a little longer than the last. Gormshuil enters only the day it came and the count of names.

title: The vote for a light at Cuan ruadh
summary: After two boats are lost on the harbour rocks in a winter fog, the town council of Cuan ruadh votes its own coal money to burn a light on the mole where no Board light has ever reached.

title: Comhairle nan Taighean-solais's refusal
summary: The Comhairle nan Taighean-solais writes back to Cuan ruadh that its charter names five lights and no more, and that the town's own light, being no charge on An Crùn, may continue as it is. Gormshuil enters the refusal in four lines.

title: The rules of the first Còmhrag
summary: The first Còmhrag at Ceann leathan is fought under rules that run to little more than a fee, a bar on edged weapons, and a purse for the last man standing inside the ropes. Nobody thinks the custom will need more than that.

title: The dead of the first Còmhrag buried
summary: Two men who do not walk out of the ropes at the first Còmhrag are buried at Ceann leathan within the week. Còmhrag Ceann leathan is fought again the following summer regardless, and the record gives their deaths one plain sentence.

title: Calum Ruadh's purse counted out
summary: A year's wages are counted out on a trestle table by the fair-wardens' own clerk for Calum mac Aonghais, hewer of Muileann chrom, who wins the first Còmhrag by refusing to stay down.

title: The right to bear arms entered on the shire's roll
summary: Calum Ruadh's right to bear arms in any shire of the kingdom, Còmhrag Ceann leathan's second prize, is entered that same evening on the shire's roll at Ceann leathan, a right his own father never held.

title: The fair-wardens' free table
summary: The inn-keepers of Ceann leathan, four of whom built new houses that year for Còmhrag Ceann leathan's crowds, keep Calum Ruadh's table free of charge, a custom nobody formally agrees to but that holds for as long as he comes back to fight.

title: Gormshuil's mother laughs at the idiom
summary: Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's mother, hearing in her village by Ceann àrsaidh that her daughter has let mar a thàinig Niall into the royal record, laughs longer than Gormshuil thinks the thing deserves, and says her daughter spent years learning to write like nobody in particular so that she could in the end write like everybody.

title: Nine generations named at Seann Dunn
summary: At the first naming in the hall at Seann Dunn an old woman of the town recites nine generations of her dead before her voice gives out, and her son speaks the tenth for her.

title: Calum Ruadh walks home alone
summary: Calum Ruadh walks out of Ceann leathan before dawn the morning after the first Còmhrag with the purse in his coat and the shire clerk's paper folded inside it, past the shuttered inns and the field where the ropes were taken down in the night, and takes Rathad na Mèinne north toward Muileann chrom alone.
